children.text: The various symbols stamped in a passport can be very confusing, especially if you haven't encountered them before. When entering different countries, if a border officer writes certain symbols or a code on your passport at the border, it means you have some kind of violation and are not being granted entry into the country. The reasons behind such violations are often hidden precisely behind these codes.
A
(No valid travel document): means that at the time of travel, you don't have a valid travel document with you — for example, an expired or invalid passport.
B

(False/counterfeit/forged travel document): if you find this code in your passport, it means the border officer considered your travel document, your passport, to be fake, which is a fairly serious accusation and requires further explanation.
C
(No valid visa or residence permit): this symbol is written when your passport doesn't contain a valid visa or residence permit, which is required for entry into the country.
D

(False/counterfeit/forged visa or residence permit): if the border officer marked the letter D in your passport, it means your travel document, such as your visa or residence card, is invalid or forged.
E

(No appropriate documentation justifying the purpose and conditions of stay): while traveling, if you're unable to confirm the purpose of your trip to the border officer, and also fail to present the required documentation, the letter E will be marked in your passport.
F

(Has already stayed for three months during a six-month period on the territory of the Member States of the European Union): this symbol indicates that you've already spent three months in an EU member country and don't have the right to stay any longer.
G
(Does not have sufficient means of subsistence): this symbol indicates that the border officer has doubts about your financial resources.
H

(Is a person for whom an alert has been issued for the purposes of refusing entry): his symbol indicates that your entry into the country is already restricted for certain reasons. This may be due to reasons recorded in the SIS (Schengen Information System) or in a national registry.
I

(Is considered to be a threat to public policy, internal security, public health or the international relations of one or more of the Member States of the European Union): among those listed, the letter I is the most serious, meaning that your entry poses a threat to public order, security, health, or international relations.

page.title: What Can the Symbols Written in Your Passport Mean?

children.text: If a symbol like this is written on you at the border, you must determine the reason behind it. In such a case, you can contact the relevant authorities or a consul to find out what the problem is and how it might be resolved. In addition, it's important to always have valid and correct documentation: your passport, visa, financial documents, and so on.
Always check your documents before traveling: make sure your passport and visa are valid.
If you've had any issue or restriction in the past, seek consultation with the relevant authority in advance.
Be attentive and understand that such symbols at the border are the start of an unpleasant process, and resolving the issue will require time and patience.

The codes stamped in a passport may seem like a minor detail at first glance, but they point to serious issues we may run into while traveling. It's important that your documents are in order when presenting them at the border, and that you're prepared for the border officer's questions. This will allow you to avoid such misunderstandings and involvement in procedures such as an appeal. If you find any such symbol in your passport, it's best not to waste time and to contact the relevant authority to find out how the issue can be resolved.
